name: LINEST
description: LINEST returns an array of statistics that describe a least-squares linear regression, including the slope and intercept, and optionally full regression diagnostics. It is an array function.
tldr: Returns regression statistics (slope, intercept, and more) as an array.

parameters.name: known_ys
parameters.description: The dependent (y) values of the known data.

parameters.name: known_xs
parameters.description: The independent (x) values; for multiple regression supply several columns. Defaults to 1,2,3,... if omitted.

parameters.name: const
parameters.description: TRUE (or omitted) includes an intercept; FALSE forces the line through the origin.

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: FALSE (or omitted) returns just slope and intercept; TRUE adds standard errors, R-squared, F, df, and sums of squares.

basicExample.description: Get slope and intercept of a fitted line
basicExample.explanation: The fitted line is y = -1 + 2.2x, so LINEST returns slope 2.2 and intercept -1 (entered as an array in two cells).

advancedExamples.title: Full regression statistics
advancedExamples.scenario: Need diagnostics, not just the line
advancedExamples.description: Set stats to TRUE for a 2-row by 5-column array
advancedExamples.explanation: Row 1 is slope, intercept, standard error of slope, standard error of intercept, R-squared. Row 2 is standard error of y, F-statistic, degrees of freedom, regression sum of squares, residual sum of squares. In older Excel enter with Ctrl+Shift+Enter; in Microsoft 365 it spills.

advancedExamples.title: Multiple regression
advancedExamples.result: Array of coefficients for both x-columns plus intercept and diagnostics
advancedExamples.explanation: With n x-columns, LINEST returns n+1 coefficients in the first row (one slope per column, then the intercept).

howItWorks: LINEST performs ordinary least-squares regression, minimizing the sum of squared residuals. With a single x it fits y = a + bx and returns the slope and intercept (and, with stats=TRUE, the full diagnostic block). With multiple x-columns it returns one slope per column plus the intercept. Because it is an array function, the results spill into adjacent cells.

howToSteps.name: Select output area
howToSteps.text: For stats=TRUE, select a 2-row by 5-column range; otherwise two cells.

howToSteps.name: Enter formula
howToSteps.text: Type =LINEST(known_ys, known_xs, TRUE, TRUE) and press Enter (or Ctrl+Shift+Enter in legacy Excel).

howToSteps.name: Read results
howToSteps.text: Use the slope/intercept to build the equation; use R-squared and F to judge fit.

limitations: Returns an array, so in pre-dynamic Excel it must be entered as an array formula with enough empty cells to spill into.
known_xs and known_ys must have the same number of rows, or #REF! is returned.
If the x-columns are linearly dependent, the function returns #REF! because the regression cannot be solved.

commonErrors.cause: Array sizes mismatch or the x-columns are collinear (linearly dependent).
commonErrors.fix: Match row counts and remove redundant/duplicate x-columns.

commonErrors.cause: Output range too small or not entered as an array.
commonErrors.fix: Select a large enough range and use Ctrl+Shift+Enter (legacy Excel).

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: LINEST works as an array function in Google Sheets with the same layout and diagnostics.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Identical behavior and array layout to Excel.

faq.question: What does the basic LINEST return?
faq.answer: Just two values: the slope and the intercept of the fitted line, in that order.

faq.question: How do I get R-squared and other stats?
faq.answer: Set the fourth argument (stats) to TRUE to add standard errors, R-squared, F, df, and sums of squares.

faq.question: How is LINEST related to SLOPE/INTERCEPT/FORECAST?
faq.answer: SLOPE, INTERCEPT, and FORECAST use the same least-squares line; LINEST returns all of it (plus diagnostics) in one array.
